security_audit.summary: Static hits are largely documentation examples, Markdown formatting, placeholder secrets, and explicit CLI usage. No prompt injection or hidden malware behavior was found. Contextual risks remain around Anthropic evaluation data handling and unsafe file-resource examples.

remediation.issue: Evaluation harness can send tool outputs to Anthropic.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before evaluation and advise redacting private data from questions, tool schemas, and tool results.

remediation.issue: Resource examples show path construction from user-controlled names.
remediation.suggestion: Add path normalization, base-directory enforcement, and examples that reject traversal sequences before reading files.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Data Sent To Third-Party Model
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation harness sends questions, tool schemas, and tool results to Anthropic through client.messages.create. This can expose sensitive data returned by an MCP server during evaluation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly calls client.messages.create with messages and tools, then appends serialized tool results to later model calls. The behavior is expected for evaluation, but data handling needs clear disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: Path Traversal Risk In Resource Examples
semantic_findings.description: The resource examples build document paths or resource names from URI parameters without showing normalization or directory checks. Users who copy these examples could expose files outside the intended document directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly derive file/resource names from URI input without validation. They are documentation examples, so active exploitability is lower than executable code.

content.value_statement: MCP integrations are hard to design well because agents need concise, reliable tools. This skill guides research, implementation, review, and evaluation for Python and TypeScript MCP servers.
actual_capabilities: Explains agent-centered MCP tool design principles.
Guides Python FastMCP server setup and tool registration.
Guides Node and TypeScript server setup with Zod validation.
Provides review checklists for errors, pagination, and response size.
Includes an evaluation workflow and a Python harness.
Points to official MCP and SDK documentation for current details.
limitations: Does not generate a complete server without user input.
Requires external documentation for service-specific API details.
Evaluation harness sends prompts and tool outputs to Anthropic.
Some resource examples need stronger path safety before reuse.

use_cases.title: Plan a new integration
use_cases.description: Map service workflows, authentication needs, and tool boundaries before implementation.

use_cases.title: Implement a server
use_cases.description: Build Python or TypeScript MCP tools with validation, pagination, and clear errors.

use_cases.title: Evaluate tool quality
use_cases.description: Create read-only tasks and run an evaluation report against a local or remote server.

prompt_templates.title: Plan my MCP server
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an MCP server for [service]. Identify workflows, tools, auth, response formats, and testing needs.

prompt_templates.title: Design tool schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed MCP tools and improve names, inputs, annotations, errors, and pagination. Service context: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Implement in Python
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python guide to build a FastMCP server for [service]. Include Pydantic models, async API helpers, and concise responses.

prompt_templates.title: Create evaluations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create ten stable read-only evaluation questions for this MCP server. Verify each answer and remove tasks requiring writes.

output_examples.input: I need a GitHub MCP server for issue triage.
output: A workflow plan covering issue search, labeling, assignment, and summary tools.
Suggested read-only and write-capable tool boundaries.
Evaluation questions for common triage tasks.

output_examples.input: My TypeScript MCP server returns too much data.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends pagination, concise defaults, and truncation messages that tell agents how to request more specific results.

output_examples.input: I want to test a server before release.
output: A read-only evaluation plan with stable questions.
A run command for the provided evaluation harness.
A review checklist for failed tasks and tool feedback.

best_practices: Start from user workflows, then choose API endpoints.
Use strict input validation and clear error messages for every tool.
Keep evaluation tasks read-only, stable, and independently verifiable.
anti_patterns: Wrapping every API endpoint as a separate tool without workflow design.
Returning large unfiltered payloads by default.
Copying file resource examples without path validation.

faq.question: Does this skill create MCP servers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning, implementation, review, and evaluation. You still provide service details and code changes.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Python with FastMCP and Node or TypeScript with the MCP SDK.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Some steps fetch official MCP and SDK documentation. The evaluation harness also calls Anthropic when you run it.

faq.question: Is the evaluation harness required?
faq.answer: No. It is optional, but useful for measuring whether tools solve real tasks.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing?
faq.answer: Review authentication, input validation, path safety, rate limits, and whether tool outputs expose sensitive data.
